text:
leo: Noticed flaky trace links in staging. When the Python async client retries, X-Request-Id and trace headers change between attempts.

anya: Repro?

leo: Minimal: set a ContextVar op id, middleware writes X-Request-Id from it, then call client that retries once. Attempt 1 has traceparent & X-Request-Id op-7a, attempt 2 shows different X-Request-Id and missing traceparent.

anya: Sounds like we apply injectors only on the initial path and we re-run middleware per attempt (generating new ids). Two fixes: compute operation-level headers once before retry loop; keep attempt-level metadata applied per try.

leo: Agreed. Proposal: add AsyncClient(..., preserve_operation_headers=False) opt-in. If True, SDK will compute injected headers (OTEL + request-id) once and merge into every retry. Also expose a typed AsyncRequestHook Protocol in redwood.sdk.types to make middleware implementers happy.

anya: Good plan. Devex sample should show opentelemetry.inject usage and how to enable the flag. Small unit test idea: monkeypatch transport.send to fail first call then succeed and assert headers identical across calls.

ci-bot: Issue created: DEVEX-4722 "async sdk: preserve operation headers across retries + typing for hooks" assigned to @anya.

leo: I'll open a small PR with tests and a short doc blurb for onboarding.

anya: Thanks — will review. :thumbsup:
